# Three-App hosted PR burst, 2026-11-17

Completed the 30-PR workload. Protected merge and edit-preservation checks passed.
All 27 disjoint edits and exactly one shared-file
proposal landed through the protected merge queue. The other two shared-file
PRs remain open with their original heads and a real Git add/add conflict.
No edits were silently dropped and no conflict was resolved automatically.

## Workload and identities

The recovery branch was `codex/mit-lit-recovery`, starting at
`645f81cee19a49e4b70bdc67c21903b75a5e1770`. Its source ancestry remains the MIT baseline
`98c59bb2dbebcf7f575993a4ad89e1300a578c83`. v1.8.0 remained a black-box executable.
Only its `--version` was read during this qualification.

`host-a` (Linux x86_64), `host-e` and `host-f` (Linux arm64) each used a distinct
private GitHub App, a sandbox-only installation token, ten isolated worktrees,
and three concurrent publishers. All proposals were pinned to
`c9143f60939aeac776764f9ced1b65df1de6518f`. The host receipts record a publication window of
16.3 seconds. This is an operational trial,
not a controlled throughput benchmark or 30 independent agent identities.

All 30 PRs were queued before `main` advanced. Observed peak queue depth was
30, with
23 simultaneous merge-group runs.
Temporary build capacity changed from 1 to 6, then 30, and finally back to 1.
The required check stayed `Agent workflow candidate`, bound to the GitHub
Actions integration 15368. Main retained no bypass actors, ALLGREEN, and one
entry per merge. All five rulesets' writable settings were restored and read
back after the run. The temporary burst refs are now covered by the catch-all.

## Verification

- All 30 automatic `pull_request` checks succeeded. No manual statuses or
  manually dispatched workflows were used.
- Each successful PR check ran the six batch regressions and the 10-worker
  fixture. Its synthetic merge checkout and App-authored proposal head were
  recorded separately.
- Each of the 28 landed commits matched its successful `merge_group` check
  SHA, checked-out SHA, timeline merge event, and Git first-parent history.
  Each queue check ran the six batch regressions and the 10/50/100-worker
  fixtures. Check provenance was GitHub Actions, with no manual statuses on
  any checked or proposal SHA.
- Each merged commit had the expected proposal as its second parent and
  changed only its assigned path. All final file bytes matched the original
  proposal, including the single shared-file winner.
- GitHub rejected all nine genuine fast-forward attempts against peer refs
  and main with branch-rule errors. All target refs remained unchanged.
- Both losing shared-file heads remain intact. `git merge-tree --write-tree`
  independently returned add/add conflicts against final main.
- Each host revoked its installation token and removed temporary worktrees
  and source directories. The three downloaded PEM files were removed from
  the operator host. The App installations and their registered public keys
  remain. Each App now has three key registrations, including two from the
  earlier pilot. No private signing files are retained by this trial.

Final main is `4860f47935e97f4959e5968d79ab22195bad6a20`.

## Queue cleanup finding

The fully automatic queue-cleanup criterion did **not** pass. PR #39 left the
queue automatically after the shared-file winner merged. PR #41 remained in
`UNMERGEABLE` queue state, with no candidate commit and PR mergeability
`UNKNOWN`, for several minutes. Native Git independently confirmed its
add/add conflict. The initial final-state verification failed on the unknown
mergeability and its adverse log is preserved.

The operator explicitly withdrew #41 after recording this state. No statuses
were posted, no workflows were dispatched, and neither main nor the proposal
head changed. The remaining open PR then reported its conflict normally.
A production coordinator should detect and safely withdraw stale unmergeable
entries, fence cleanup against the expected proposal head, and reconcile
unknown outcomes after restart. This trial establishes protected merge safety
with operator-assisted queue cleanup, not a fully unattended hosted workflow.

## Evidence and limits

Full proposal SHAs, check IDs, run URLs, identity receipts and denied ref
updates are in [the machine-readable results](app-burst-results-2026-11-17.json).
The reusable publisher is [app-burst-worker.py](app-burst-worker.py). The local
API responses, job logs, Git verification and restored-rule readbacks are at
`<private-path>`.

This qualifies three authenticated App identities, 30 real PRs, branch ownership,
automatic checks and conflict exclusion for this workload. GitHub-hosted CI
ran the recovery binary on Ubuntu. The lab hosts ran Git publishers. This run
does not requalify the complete regression suite, native macOS or arm64 binary
semantics, scheduler fencing after task reassignment, or restart/duplicate
submission recovery across the hosted control plane.
